pr_text:
retro(R-MAIN): W1-1b Sentry transaction scrub, W1-1c /admin Basic 500 -> 401, W1-9c async-aware default limiter, W1-10b windowed loop-lag max

W1-1b (security, unflagged): init_sentry now passes before_send_transaction. It runs the same request-region scrub as before_send (X-Admin-Key / Authorization / Cookie headers, the URL and raw query_string PII, request data/cookies) through one shared helper, _scrub_request_region, so the two hooks cannot drift. Before this, every sampled performance transaction for an authenticated admin request shipped X-Admin-Key verbatim (the SDK's own filter does not list it). Trace ids, spans and contexts are untouched, and 503 transactions are NOT dropped.

W1-1c (security, unflagged): the /admin/* static mount's Basic branch catches (ValueError, UnicodeError). b64decode(str) raises a plain ValueError on a raw >= 0x80 byte, and binascii.Error is a subclass of ValueError, so the old clause missed it and the mount 500'd. `Basic \xff\xfe` now returns 401 + WWW-Authenticate. The try wraps only the decode, so a serving error on an authenticated request is not turned into a 401.

W1-9c (inside ENABLE_DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITS, default OFF): under the flag the app registers slowapi's SlowAPIASGIMiddleware instead of SlowAPIMiddleware. On pinned slowapi 0.1.10, SlowAPIMiddleware cannot await our async handler, so its 429s shipped a bare {"error": ...} body. With the ASGI variant, /health, / and /favicon.ico 429 with the envelope, code RATE_LIMITED, and Retry-After. With the flag OFF the app is byte-identical: no middleware, pinned by fresh exec. Measured limit on the pinned stack: slowapi's _find_route_handler cannot see through fastapi 0.141's _IncludedRouter entries, so the blanket default reaches ONLY the app-level routes. CLAUDE.md correction: the ENABLE_DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITS row's '21 routes' claim is false on the pinned stack. Widening the limit to router routes is follow-up W1-9d, because it would rate-limit every client at 10/min.

W1-10b (additive key): /health and loop_lag_snapshot() gain loop_lag_max_60s_ms, the max over a 60-slot ring of per-tick lag samples floored at 0. The recorder recomputes it, so /health stays a dict read. loop_lag_max_ms is a high-water mark since process start that never decays, so a new stall after an old one was invisible. The existing keys are unchanged.

W1-7b: tests/test_retro_w1_7_w1_10.py makes the loop-lag pins non-vacuous. A synthetic tick is read back through GET /health without the heartbeat overwriting it. The heartbeat records now - previous and advances previous. The shutdown handler is registered. tests/test_health_loop_lag.py is intentionally untouched: its vacuous nodes are backstopped by these mutation-verified pins.

Fixer round: the wip commit b519f9de carried a 59-slot ring (maxlen=LOOP_LAG_WINDOW_SLOTS - 1), a mutant left on disk by the killed green. The committed test file already fails on it (test_window_is_exactly_sixty_ticks). This change restores the 60-slot ring and adds test_window_of_only_short_ticks_reads_zero_not_negative, which kills the surviving unfloored-ring mutant. Mutation matrix: 13 of 14 killed. The one survivor is the unfloored ring against the committed tests, which is exactly why the new pin was added; that mutant is killed by the current tests. The comm gate on 61 files shows the same failure set as base 1c6f6796 (9 netguard DNS casualties, all present at base).
